reference: Literal synthetic-proc contracts for the custom procps-shaped API, independently checked fixture totals, units and row layouts. Version identity and Bash metadata are custom contracts. These cases do not establish numerical equivalence to procps-ng; shared-procfs/clock comparison is still needed for guest accounting, swap-page scaling and fractional uptime.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and short help metadata
Fork count and summary field ordering, memory-unit conversion, CPU and VM counters
Wide active/inactive snapshot layout, since-boot averages, and zero-delay delta sample
Per-device and aggregate diskstats output plus partition filtering
exclusions: Live host procfs is never read; operation contracts use only relative synthetic files via BASHOS_PROC_ROOT.
Nonzero-delay sampling against changing procfs, timestamp behavior, long-count header cadence, and live kernel counters are deferred to a disposable VM or controlled procfs/clock mock.

Guest-time accounting, swap page-size/rate conversion, summary used-memory definitions and fractional-uptime numerical equivalence with procps-ng remain unqualified. The literal synthetic snapshots are custom API contracts, not proof of those external semantics.

cases.purpose: Check the documented implementation identity without impersonating an external procps-ng release.
Verify Bash exposes vmstat as a loadable builtin without invoking a system-information operation.
Check the short usage string against the vmstat builtin's documented Bash help metadata.
Read the forks counter from a private synthetic proc/stat file and verify procps-style numeric formatting.
Verify the documented -s labels, ordering, raw event counters, and decimal-kilobyte conversion from deterministic proc files.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'cpu 100 20 30 400 5 6 7 8 9 10' 'intr 1234 5 6' 'ctxt 2345' 'btime 1111111111' 'processes 321' 'procs_running 2' 'procs_blocked 1' > stat
printf '%s\n' 'pgpgin 600' 'pgpgout 700' 'pswpin 12' 'pswpout 13' > vmstat
printf '%s\n' 'MemTotal: 2048 kB' 'MemFree: 512 kB' 'Buffers: 128 kB' 'Cached: 256 kB' 'Active: 768 kB' 'Inactive: 384 kB' 'SwapTotal: 1024 kB' 'SwapFree: 768 kB' > meminfo
BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=. vmstat -s -S k

cases.purpose: Exercise wide columns, -a memory labels, decimal-kilobyte scaling, since-boot CPU percentages/rates, and a second zero-delay sample with counter deltas.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' 'cpu 100 20 30 400 5 6 7 8 9 10' 'intr 1234 5 6' 'ctxt 2345' 'btime 1111111111' 'processes 321' 'procs_running 2' 'procs_blocked 1' > stat
printf '%s\n' 'pgpgin 600' 'pgpgout 700' 'pswpin 12' 'pswpout 13' > vmstat
printf '%s\n' 'MemTotal: 2048 kB' 'MemFree: 512 kB' 'Buffers: 128 kB' 'Cached: 256 kB' 'Active: 768 kB' 'Inactive: 384 kB' 'SwapTotal: 1024 kB' 'SwapFree: 768 kB' > meminfo
printf '%s\n' '10.50 0.00' > uptime
BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=. vmstat -a -w -S k 0 2

cases.purpose: Check per-device diskstats headers, field selection, integer units, row ordering, and skipping of a malformed record.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '8 0 sda 10 2 300 40 5 1 600 70 3 8000 9000' 'malformed record' '8 1 sda1 5 1 100 20 4 1 400 50 2 6000 7000' > diskstats
BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=. vmstat -d
cases.stdout:

disk          total merged sectors      ms  total merged sectors      ms    cur    sec
sda              10      2     300      40      5      1     600      70      3      8
sda1              5      1     100      20      4      1     400      50      2      6
